curation.notes: Tethered-ligand single-molecule force spectroscopy of the SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 RBD:ACE2 interaction using two complementary custom-built instruments: AFM at constant loading rate (sawtooth pattern of interface opening, partial RBD unfolding and stepwise ACE2 unfolding, anchored by an ultrastable ClfA:Fg-gamma handle) and magnetic tweezers at constant force for equilibrium measurements, complemented by steered MD. Constructs based on PDB 2ajf and 6m0j with 85-aa (31 nm) or 115-aa (42 nm) interdomain linkers; soluble ACE2 used as a blocking agent.

evidence.snippet: Measurements of tethered ligand constructs in AFM and MT were performed in TBS (25 mM Tris, 72 mM NaCl, 1 mM CaCl2 at pH 7.2 and 22 °C).
AFM force-extension trace of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD:ACE2 tethered ligand construct (raw data in light green, total variation denoised in dark green, recorded at 800 nm/s retraction velocity).

handle_sequences.annotations: a longer linker (115 amino acids [aa] corresponding to 42 nm contour length, instead of 85 aa or 31 nm) between the two domains

evidence.snippet: To test blocking, recombinant human ACE2 (GLN18-SER740, C-terminal His-tag) from RayBiotech (∼3.8 µM in measurement buffer, # 230-30165-100) was flushed into the flow cell and briefly incubated before the measurement.
The last (rightmost) peak exhibits forces well within the range previously established for the ultrastrong ClfA:Fgɣ interaction (18), clearly indicating specific attachment of the protein construct.
